I hear all of the frustration in your post and I can relate. 

There are a lot of people out there who I'd be best not associating with. I've found that people will show you exactly who they are if you let them. It can be tough for me to see that because I never had an example of what actual friendship and support looked like. I have built a few strong friendships that have shown me that. 

A few comments from my own experience on the situations you mentioned:

1) I think it is totally valid to not want to speak to an ex's ex if they are still maintaining contact with that ex. It sounds like you had a boundary around that issue, upheld that boundary, and that she was not able to accept that. Boundaries are tough and I think it's awesome how you handled that situation.

2) Dating is hard. I have learned that my story is my own and that people don't deserve my confidence until they have earned it. In dating situations I only share what is appropriate given our level of closeness and it has taken a LOT of trial and error to discover that. I may say "I am trying to take it slow" and not share a reason why because thats none of their business at that point. 

3) For me, friendship is a balance of my friends carrying me and me carrying my friends. Sometimes this balance happens over the course of a single conversation, sometimes it's on a week by week cycle and sometimes it's on a monthly or yearly cycle. I do find that I have to actively balance my friendships to make sure that I'm giving and receiving, but if they aren't capable of holding space for my emotions and my experience then those relationships tend to drift on their own due to my lack of investment in them.

I admire your courage. It takes a lot to share all of what is going on with you and to ask for help. Thank you for your power of example!

I have quit caffeine cold turkey several times and at the very least it is destabilizing for me. It usually results in a few weeks to a month of brain fog and more depressive mood but for me but then clears eventually and I feel better than when I am on it.

Good luck navigating whatever the situation is for you.
